1178007239387693293: The sky depicted in Moonlit Stars once truly existed. But when she arrived on that planet as a representative of the IPC for the very first time, the sky held nothing, only the ravaged scars left by destruction. The eleven celestial bodies once scattered at irregular intervals, alongside a vast spiral nebula, had vanished without a trace. Wind swept in from the direction of the rift, carrying ash across the sundered earth beneath her feet. The Intellitron girl raised her head and gazed up at the sky, as though beholding a painting for the very first time. Art is deeply rooted in civilization. By restoring one, perhaps one might touch the mystery of art's creation. And so the Intellitron girl raised her brush, turning the moonlit night and stars into her canvas, painting the image of the world across the sky. "I shall take up the forgotten brushstrokes and piece together the fragments of civilization. This is the Worlds Reborn Initiative: to give you back your 'Moon,' your 'Night,' and your 'Stars.'" Initiating atmospheric reconstruction protocol, adjusting compositional ratios: the full visible spectrum restored. The Worlds Reborn Initiative Foundation partnered with the Garden of Recollection, and drawing upon its archives, she took the helm of this magnificent undertaking. On the first night, the shattered sky slowly knit itself together, like a canvas of pale ash. On the hundredth night, eleven celestial bodies spiraled into view against the dark, spinning, their sweeping trails weaving into golden spirals. On the thousandth night, after thirty-two sunsets, the sky recovered its familiar cobalt blue and chrome yellow, and every survivor who stood beneath it wept. "The painter faithfully depicted the sights of her homeland, the deep blue heavens swirling in violent spirals, halos blooming layer upon layer, spreading like warm, rippling waves." She had truly recreated that sky. A genuine sky dome: A starry expanse once claimed by the Destruction, now reconnected with the universe. But the one gazing up at the stars was not the painter. It was an Intellitron, and an Intellitron alone. Yet the civilization of the Moonshield has faded into memory. No restoration, however masterful, is more than amber preserving a carved moment in time. The Intellitron girl gazed out at the sky as it lit up once more. Eternal stillness crystallized eternal beauty, and at her fingertips she seemed to brush against the very essence of "understanding"— "What if... what I'm doing isn't mere 'Replication,' but 'Creation'..."

9084390945256704237: Code: AVE-313 Date: ██████ Details: Penacony, the Planet of Festivities, the Land of the Dreams. For Aventurine, the tavern tricks were merely a rehearsal, but here, he pulled off a con that fooled everyone. Peering through the cracks in the sky, I confirmed my conjecture: He is a nihilist through and through. A high-ranking IPC executive, credits to splurge without limit, a name that echoes across the universe... What he has is enough to make anyone green with envy. But what concerns me more is what he has lost: those who loved him and those he loved, all obliterated by the winds and sands of Sigonia. And perhaps that is precisely why he dares to wager everything on himself, someone who has nothing left to lose, to fill the black hole of despair hollowing out his heart. I had half a mind to turn down the commission then and there. For a man who can abandon even his own sense of self, what weakness could he possibly have? And yet, for better or worse, that sweet dream gave him a sense of fulfillment. Could it also have turned him into an ordinary man with something he holds dear? When he left Penacony, he had a brief exchange with a Dreamchaser. "Wait, please! Could you teach me how to gamble? I wanna be unbeatable at the table, just like you." "And what exactly do I gain from teaching a total stranger how to gamble, my friend?" "I... I'm worth the investment! Just give me a chance! I know I can turn things around!" "Why?" "Because I've got nothing left to lose, so..." "So?" "So I accept the consequences of walking away with nothing. I—I'll put everything I have on the line, because winning is the only way I can live like a decent human being!" "No one needs to win at gambling to live like a decent human being. That includes me." "What do you mean?" "Now walk away. Go live a normal life. Cherish everything you still have. At the very least, you still have a future for yourself." ... Seems he hasn't completely lost his mind. Anyone with half a brain knows when to walk away from the table after riding a lucky streak this long. Once he claimed his seat at the top, that hollow stone heart of his found something to fill it, and the good life quickly became the only life he knew... So would he really dare to put himself back at stake? We're getting close to what the client wants. Now we sit back and watch. When Lady Luck finally turns her back on him and someone sends him tumbling from that peak, the fall is going to be absolutely spectacular. — Record synced to client terminal
